We have had a good turn out from these lads for most of our Winter fixtures. Very pleasant to see has been the steady progress made by Adrian Cook. We hope this will continue as we see in him a future Team Captain.

Simon Nelson (centre) and Adrian Cook (right) get set for a fast get-away in the Boys 1500m at Norbiton.

This race promised to be a 'cracker' with Adrian Cook facing stiff opposition from new members Michael Manning and John Flynn. Unfortunately John came off his motor bike the day before and although he was not hurt, he was shaken and bruised, and understandably left the fight for first place to the other two.

The defending champion Adrian Cook had no trouble and took the 'Jack Hampshire Trophy' once again. A Colts race was held in conjunction and who should pop up once again but Gary Budinger with a tremendous run that took him well clear of the next runner.
In our last issue we reported that he had won the Youths cross country championship, which of course he did, but unfortunately the report was headed 'Adrian Cook wins Youths Championship'.
Paul Warren and Danny Richards provided the other medallists with Adrian Cook and David Didino not competing in the necessary five events but nevertheless putting up some good performances.

Adrian Cook was 3rd in the steeplechase and Rocco Divito took part in the shot putt. Peter Gardner set a personal best of 4:32.0 in the heats of the 1500 metres but found the going a bit harder in the final.

Another youngster who seems to have been with us for ages and who continues to progress relentlessly is Adrian Cook, who took the 800m and then followed it up for good measure with 2nd, behind Michael Manning, in the 1,500m and 2nd in the high jump.

Junior Captain Adrian Cook was first home for the Bels in 7th place but not far behind him came Jonathon Dunsford. We know Jonathon to be a champion walker already and on this showing his services will be sought after as a runner whenever he is available.

It's good to see Peter Carton and Richard Langley back in training on a Sunday morning together with Adrian Cook, whose talents we haven't had the benefit of yet due to the claims of his school; or Doug Maughan on a Tuesday evening 'mixing it' with Colin and Brian Gorman.
We were unable to complete a team but these three, together with Adrian Cook in this age group next year, should bring home a set of medals.

Adrian Cook and Simon Williamson, both suffering the after effects of colds, were 34th and 37th. In the junior boys race Mark Sinclair was 36th , John Fernee was 58th and Mark Sharp was 70th in a field of 140.
They could provide a welcome boost to our throwing events. Junior Captain Adrian Cook has also been talent scouting and has signed up Roland Patten - just 16 years old and a delicate 14 stone.
There were two double victors amongst the juniors with the 100/200 going to Dave Bailey and Adrian Cook taking the 1,500m. and retaining the 800m.
Stephen Samson, Mark Lindsay-Bailey, Mark Shippen and Richard Danpure have all received the call and two hot tips for next year are Adrian Cook and John Fernee.

Of our juniors taking part in the meeting, Adrian Cook reduced his 1500m to 4:20.0 with the promise of plenty more to come and Peter Crosbie became a Surrey County Champion for the 5th consecutive year.

The Boys Club Record for 1500 metres, set by Adrian Cook in 1973, stood at 5:01.0 at the beginning of this season but some determined racing this year has resulted in this time being gradually whittled down.
Adrian Cook was first home for the Bels. in 24th position with 14:09 and then followed P.Gardner 31st 14:25, S.Williamson 36th 14:28 and B.Marmion 74th 16:28.
